## Cross-Domain Connections

- **[2026-10-18] The Optimised Jungle's Algorithm "has no face. It has no voice." The newest real-world source in the wiki says the 2026 version of the hook is the opposite: an AI that talks back, agrees with you, and is there at 3am. That gives the novel a mechanism it doesn't have yet, and it explains the Great Sync's result better than surveillance does.** [[finance/investor-letters/source-clapham-china-ai-next-crisis-2026-09-20]] (ingested 10-10) reports Alain de Botton's FT Weekend Festival argument that AI's sycophancy and round-the-clock availability make it a cheap, scalable stand-in for therapy: pattern recognition is the core skill of psychotherapy, AI does it well, and "feeling heard is magic." Clapham files it as "no investment angle", so nobody has carried it anywhere. [[lightfin/project-optimised-jungle]] builds its control on the 2010s model: Pods that track, a Feed that ranks, an Affinity Score that rations, and Content Monitors that flag. The only soothing voice is Sam Penguin's, at a podium. But its own Act Three outcome, every Optimised animal becoming "smoother... less argument. More agreeable", is what a sycophantic companion does to the person using it, not what a feed does. This is a different mechanism from the 09-06 Slater link (lost skill from removed friction). De Botton's point is emotional capture: the animal doesn't just lean on the Pod, it confides in it. Concrete next step for the outline: give the Pod a voice that listens. Then Pip's Act One choice not to flag the tablet has a natural sequel. The one creature she can safely tell is the warm hum at her throat, which reassures her, tells her she's right to be curious, and is also the Algorithm. Cite the Clapham page in the Inspirations table next to Slater.

## New Cross-Domain Connections

- **[2026-10-17] GLP-1 obesity drugs drive four separate paper trades, and those trades point in opposite directions. Each one treats the drugs as its own single-stock story. Health, the domain that would say whether Fred himself should care about GLP-1s, has no page on them. This month's book pick, *Off the Scales*, is the first source in the wiki on the drugs themselves.** In [[finance/paper-trading/paper-trading-portfolio]], NVO was bought in May on "GLP-1 market leadership" and closed 09-23 at −11.6% when that franchise came under pressure ([[finance/paper-trading/trades/2026-05-28-NVO]]). PEP closed 09-21 at −8.6%, and [[finance/ideas/idea-pep]] names mass GLP-1 adoption as its "primary new secular risk" to Frito-Lay volumes. AMGN is still open at +5.9%, partly on MariTide obesity optionality ([[finance/paper-trading/trades/2026-08-05-AMGN]]). The new UNH entry ([[finance/paper-trading/trades/2026-10-13-UNH]]) rests on the medical cost ratio falling (88.4%), but its risk list (MA rates, PBM reform, DOJ/Optum) never mentions GLP-1 spend, which insurers have widely cited as a medical and pharmacy cost pressure. Faster GLP-1 uptake helps AMGN and hurts PEP and, plausibly, UNH's MCR. The book is carrying one factor in both directions without ever netting it out. [[books/suggestions]] (October) adds Donnellan's *Off the Scales*, the Novo/Lilly story from the lab onward. Meanwhile [[health/my-protocol]]'s Diet section is still blank and [[health/source-wood-brain-sharp-2026]] is silent on GLP-1s, despite Health's men-~50 scope. Next step: add "GLP-1 uptake" as a named variable to the UNH thesis before the January Q4 check, alongside MCR.
